extracted_claims.text: Article 43 provides two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems under Annex III: internal control (Annex VI) or a quality-management-system plus technical-documentation assessment involving a notified body (Annex VII), with the applicable route depending on system type and whether harmonised standards/common specifications have been applied.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric systems), providers may use internal control or a notified-body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards were applied; Annex VII (notified body) is described as mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems in some sources.

For high-risk AI systems covered by Section A of Annex I (product-safety legislation, e.g. medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures under the relevant sectoral EU legislation, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements.
A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, except for pre-determined changes in systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to authorise, by derogation from Article 43, the placing on the market of specific high-risk AI systems for a limited period, for exceptional reasons of public security, health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets.

Under Article 43, for conformity assessment under Annex VII the provider may generally choose any notified body, but where the system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions/bodies/offices/agencies, the relevant market surveillance authority under Article 74(8) or (9) acts as the notified body instead.

Annex VII specifies that notified bodies may, where necessary and after other verification means are exhausted, request access to an AI system's training and trained models (including parameters) to assess conformity, subject to IP and confidentiality protections.

Article 44 covers certificates issued following conformity assessment, Article 45 covers information obligations of notified bodies, Article 47 covers the EU declaration of conformity, and Article 48 covers CE marking, as part of Section 5 (Standards, Conformity Assessment, Certificates, Registration) of the AI Act.

A proposed amending regulation (COM(2025) 836 / 2025/0359 (COD)) would add a new Annex XIV listing codes and categories of AI systems for the purposes of notified/designated body scope under the Commission's NANDO information system, and would make related amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139.

As of late 2025/early-to-mid 2026, multiple industry sources report that no notified bodies have yet been formally designated under the EU AI Act, with designation processes still ongoing across Member States as of March and April 2026.

High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act are reported to fully apply from August 2026, after which notified bodies designated under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, intersecting with existing MDR/IVDR notified body assessments for medical device AI.

Declaration of conformity documentation for SaaS/high-risk AI providers must state which Article 43 procedure was followed (Annex VI internal control, or Annex VII with notified body), and must include notified body information where applicable, ahead of an August 2, 2026 deadline cited for SaaS providers.

As a comparison point, under the separate EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), rules on notified bodies started to apply on 11 June 2026, but as of late June 2026 zero notified bodies had been designated in NANDO for the CRA, with a target of 11 December 2026 for sufficient notified body capacity and full application from 11 December 2027.

For medical devices (MDR) and in-vitro diagnostics (IVDR), as of October 2025 the NANDO system listed 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, and the Commission publishes a list of designated notified bodies searchable by legislation in NANDO, including Member State summaries of annual monitoring reports.

Article 43(5) of the AI Act empowers the European Commission to adopt delegated acts (per Article 97) updating Annex VI (internal control procedure) and Annex VII (QMS and technical documentation assessment) in light of technical progress, without needing to revise the AI Act itself.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes administrative/identification-number requirements and lists for notified bodies under the AI Act.

contradictions.claim_b: Later AI Act Service Desk and industry sources describe Article 43 as the adopted, in-force provision of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, with specific adopted procedures (Annex VI/VII) and designated notified body mechanisms including Article 74(8)/(9) authority substitution.

contradictions.description: Source 20 explicitly states no/limited notified body designations exist as of March 2026, while source 22 discusses post-2026 notified body activity without clarifying whether any designations had actually occurred by that point, creating ambiguity about current designation status.

open_issues: No source provides a current, authoritative list of specific notified bodies formally designated under the EU AI Act (as opposed to MDR/IVDR or CRA bodies); only general statements that designation is 'ongoing' or that 'zero' have been designated in adjacent regimes (CRA) are available.

It is unclear from the sources exactly which Annex III categories beyond point 1 (biometrics) mandate the notified-body (Annex VII) route versus internal control (Annex VI), as sources give partially overlapping but not fully reconciled descriptions of 'points 2 to 8' of Annex III.

The practical interplay between AI Act notified-body designations and existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies (e.g., whether the same bodies will be dual-designated) is not clearly detailed beyond general statements that this 'will begin' post-2026.
Sources do not clarify the precise legal status or expected adoption timeline of the proposed Annex XIV amendment (COM(2025) 836) regarding notified/designated body scope codes.

The exact criteria and timeline Member States must follow to complete AI Act notified body designations are not detailed, beyond general industry commentary citing 'ongoing processes' and 'limited capacity' as of 2026.
It is unclear whether the 'August 2026' deadline cited by several sources for high-risk AI obligations is uniformly agreed upon or whether there are conflicting formal dates across sources.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems—internal control and notified-body assessment—with the applicable route depending on system category and sectoral overlaps with existing product-safety law (medium-to-low confidence across most procedural details). High-risk obligations are reported by one industry source to fully apply from August 2026, though this timeline is low confidence and not corroborated by other sources ([mdxcro](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)); meanwhile the identity and number of notified bodies actually designated under the AI Act remains unconfirmed, with sources describing designation as an ongoing, unresolved process (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act provides two routes for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III: internal control under Annex VI, or a combined quality-management-system and technical-documentation assessment involving a notified body under Annex VII, with the choice depending on system type and whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)). For biometric systems under point 1 of Annex III, providers may generally choose internal control or notified-body assessment depending on standards compliance, though some sources describe notified-body assessment as mandatory for biometric identification and critical infrastructure systems (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems)).

For high-risk systems covered by Section A of Annex I—products already regulated under sectoral EU legislation such as medical devices or machinery—providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures of that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

### Procedural Details
A new conformity assessment is required when a high-risk system is substantially modified, except for pre-determined changes in systems that continue learning post-deployment (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise, by derogation, the placing on the market of specific high-risk systems for limited periods for exceptional public-security, health, environmental, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Under Article 43, providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except where systems are intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutional use, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Annex VII allows notified bodies, as a last resort, to request access to training and trained models, including parameters, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). Related provisions include Article 44 (certificates), Article 45 (notified body information obligations), Article 47 (EU declaration of conformity), and Article 48 (CE marking) (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-60)). Article 43(5) empowers the Commission to update Annexes VI and VII via delegated acts without revising the Act itself (low confidence) ([FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)).

### August 2026 Application Timeline
One industry source reports that high-risk AI obligations are expected to fully apply from August 2026, after which AI Act-designated notified bodies would begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments alongside existing MDR/IVDR assessments for medical-device AI (low confidence) ([mdxcro](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)). A separate industry source similarly cites an August 2, 2026 deadline for SaaS providers to issue declarations of conformity specifying which Article 43 procedure (Annex VI or Annex VII) was followed (low confidence) ([sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)). These dates are not corroborated by official EU sources in the material reviewed and should be treated cautiously.

### Notified Body Designation Status
A proposed amending regulation (COM(2025) 836) would add a new Annex XIV with codes/categories for notified and designated bodies under the Commission's NANDO system (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). Industry sources report that, as of late 2025 into 2026, no notified bodies have yet been formally designated under the AI Act, with Member State processes still ongoing (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). By comparison, under the separate Cyber Resilience Act, zero notified bodies had been designated as of late June 2026 despite rules applying from 11 June 2026 (low confidence) ([CyberCertLabs](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026)). For contrast, under MDR/IVDR, NANDO listed 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies as of October 2025 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051), [European Commission](https://health.ec.europa.eu/medical-devices-topics-interest/notified-bodies-medical-devices_en)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources diverge on the legal status of Article 43: one source presents it as a 2022 proposal, while official EU guidance treats it as adopted, final law under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689—readers should rely on the latter ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43) vs. [AI proposal text](https://www.artificial-intelligence-act.com/Artificial_Intelligence_Act_Article_43_(Proposal_25.11.2022).html)). Sources also conflict on notified-body designation status, with some asserting none exist as of March 2026 and others discussing post-2026 activity without clarifying actual designation status ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act) vs. [mdxcro](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)). The August 2026 "full application" deadline is cited by two industry blogs but is not corroborated by official EU sources and is flagged as low confidence (below 0.4). Several other timeline-related claims (notified body designations) are similarly flagged as low confidence due to reliance on industry blogs rather than authoritative sources.

## Knowledge Gaps
No authoritative, current list of AI Act-designated notified bodies exists in the sources reviewed. It remains unclear exactly which Annex III categories (beyond biometrics) require notified-body versus internal-control assessment. The practical interplay between AI Act and MDR/IVDR notified bodies, the adoption timeline for the proposed Annex XIV amendment, and precise Member State designation criteria all require further research. It is also unclear whether the "August 2026" deadline cited by industry sources is a formally agreed date or whether it conflicts with other timelines, since no official EU source in the reviewed material corroborates it.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems—internal control and notified-body assessment—with the applicable route depending on system category and sectoral overlaps with existing product-safety law (medium-to-low confidence across most procedural details). However, despite high-risk obligations reportedly approaching full application, the identity and number of notified bodies actually designated under the AI Act remains unconfirmed, and available sources describe designation as an ongoing, unresolved process (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act provides two routes for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III: internal control under Annex VI, or a combined quality-management-system and technical-documentation assessment involving a notified body under Annex VII, with the choice depending on system type and whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)). For biometric systems under point 1 of Annex III, providers may generally choose internal control or notified-body assessment depending on standards compliance, though some sources describe notified-body assessment as mandatory for biometric identification and critical infrastructure systems (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems)).

For high-risk systems covered by Section A of Annex I—products already regulated under sectoral EU legislation such as medical devices or machinery—providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures of that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

### Procedural Details
A new conformity assessment is required when a high-risk system is substantially modified, except for pre-determined changes in systems that continue learning post-deployment (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise, by derogation, the placing on the market of specific high-risk systems for limited periods for exceptional public-security, health, environmental, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Under Article 43, providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except where systems are intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutional use, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Annex VII allows notified bodies, as a last resort, to request access to training and trained models, including parameters, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). Related provisions include Article 44 (certificates), Article 45 (notified body information obligations), Article 47 (EU declaration of conformity), and Article 48 (CE marking) (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-60)). Article 43(5) empowers the Commission to update Annexes VI and VII via delegated acts without revising the Act itself (low confidence) ([FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
A proposed amending regulation (COM(2025) 836) would add a new Annex XIV with codes/categories for notified and designated bodies under the Commission's NANDO system (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). Industry sources report that, as of late 2025 into 2026, no notified bodies have yet been formally designated under the AI Act, with Member State processes still ongoing (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). By comparison, under the separate Cyber Resilience Act, zero notified bodies had been designated as of late June 2026 despite rules applying from 11 June 2026 (low confidence) ([CyberCertLabs](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026)). For contrast, under MDR/IVDR, NANDO listed 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies as of October 2025 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051), [European Commission](https://health.ec.europa.eu/medical-devices-topics-interest/notified-bodies-medical-devices_en)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources diverge on the legal status of Article 43: one source presents it as a 2022 proposal, while official EU guidance treats it as adopted, final law under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689—readers should rely on the latter ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43) vs. [AI proposal text](https://www.artificial-intelligence-act.com/Artificial_Intelligence_Act_Article_43_(Proposal_25.11.2022).html)). Sources also conflict on notified-body designation status, with some asserting none exist as of March 2026 and others discussing post-2026 activity without clarifying actual designation status ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act) vs. [mdxcro](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)). Several timeline-related claims (notified body designations, August 2026 deadlines) are flagged as low confidence (below 0.4) due to reliance on industry blogs rather than authoritative sources.

## Knowledge Gaps
No authoritative, current list of AI Act-designated notified bodies exists in the sources reviewed. It remains unclear exactly which Annex III categories (beyond biometrics) require notified-body versus internal-control assessment. The practical interplay between AI Act and MDR/IVDR notified bodies, the adoption timeline for the proposed Annex XIV amendment, and precise Member State designation criteria all require further research.

Minor issue: the sentence 'Related provisions include Article 44 (certificates), Article 45..., Article 47..., and Article 48 (CE marking)' is sourced only to the article-60 link, while the underlying claim_008 also lists https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-16 as a source that is omitted from the inline citation (though listed in the Sources list).

hallucination_check.notes: No numbers or dates were found that deviate from the extracted claims (e.g., '51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies as of October 2025' matches claim_014; 'August 2026' and 'August 2, 2026' match claims_011/012; '11 June 2026'/'late June 2026' matches claim_013). All substantive statements trace back to specific claims.

contradiction_disclosure.notes: The report's 'Contradictions & Uncertainties' section correctly surfaces both known contradictions (Article 43 proposal-vs-adopted status, and conflicting notified-body designation status reports) matching the ground truth's 'Known Contradictions' list, and flags the uncorroborated August 2026 date.

confidence_assessment.notes: Confidence labels attached to each claim (e.g., 'high confidence' for claim_003 and claim_014, 'medium confidence' for claims_004-009, 'low confidence' for claims_001, 002, 010-013, 015) match the ground-truth confidence tiers.

executive_summary_accuracy.notes: The executive summary's statements about the two assessment routes, the uncorroborated August 2026 timeline, and the unresolved notified-body designation status are all substantiated in the body and carry consistent confidence framing.

knowledge_gaps.notes: The Knowledge Gaps section covers the absence of an authoritative notified-body list, ambiguity on which Annex III categories require notified-body assessment, Annex XIV timeline uncertainty, Member State designation criteria, and the unconfirmed August 2026 deadline—largely mirroring the ground truth's 'Open Issues', though it omits the specific point about AI Act/MDR-IVDR dual-designation interplay mentioned in the ground truth.
